record_type_quote: Given the ongoing debate on the underlying mechanisms and the fact that Cialdini et al.’s (1975) critical test of the alternative explanation that individuals avoid saying no twice was not statistically significant, we chose to directly replicate Cialdini et al.’s (1975) Study 3 with more precision allowed by a larger sample.

targets.authors: Cialdini, R. B., Vincent, J. E., Lewis, S. K., Catalan, J., Wheeler, D., & Darby, B. L.
targets.title: Reciprocal concessions procedure for inducing compliance: The door-in-the-face technique.
targets.evidence_quote: Given the ongoing debate on the underlying mechanisms and the fact that Cialdini et al.’s (1975) critical test of the alternative explanation that individuals avoid saying no twice was not statistically significant, we chose to directly replicate Cialdini et al.’s (1975) Study 3 with more precision allowed by a larger sample.
targets.outcome_quote: In the present article we report a direct replication of Cialdini et al.’s (1975) DITF technique. Overall, the data were consistent with the findings obtained by Cialdini et al. (1975).
targets.outcome_reasoning: Explicit overall verdict of consistency with the original decides. An exploratory exclusion analysis contrasts with one original comparison but does not outweigh this overall verdict.

reasoning: Verified title and all seven authors on accepted manuscript first page; complete article through references. One new sample directly re-tests Study 3 from one published paper.
